nsibilities:

- `card_commit_history.ts` loads/validates card activity; no execution bridge means no commits;
- `use_card_commits.ts` keys requests by `cardInternalId`, refreshes on matching root execution completion and worktree/project changes, discards stale async results after card change/unmount;
- card popup and file mode share `CardCommitMenu`/`CardCommitDiffPanel`, each with independent diff selection state;
- historical diff uses a separate read-only editor instance; whether the live editor stays mounted is an implementation detail, but historical content must never enter live editor state or persistence pipelines.

## Edge cases

- No commits from a root run: activity still records the run/conversation; icon stays hidden.
- Linked actions commit on different worktree branches: one root activity record, visibility evaluated per commit.
- Worktree commit before merge: visible while worktree valid/registered.
- Worktree removed after full merge: stays visible (reachable from primary HEAD).
- Worktree removed without merge: hidden but retained in activity.
- Commit object unavailable locally: row stays if otherwise visible; selecting shows `Commit is no longer available in this repository`.
- Root commit: old body empty, new body renders as added.
- Frontmatter-only commit: show `No body changes in this commit`, then other changed files.
- Card renamed after commit: current path may not exist at either revision; show only other changed files.
- Card deleted or surface closed while loading: discard result.
- Two local executions update one card: writer serializes writes, keeps separate `executionId` records.
- Two collaborators edit the same tracked activity file on different branches: normal Git conflict handling applies.

## Acceptance criteria

- Activity stored once per card under tracked `<projectFolder>/activity`, keyed by `cardInternalId`, written in the primary checkout regardless of execution worktree.
- One root execution creates one activity record with commits from root + all child actions, plus root action id/label and card identity.
- No path-prefix aggregation or path-derived card ownership remains.
- Conversation turns write once at terminal completion/failure/cancellation; live UI keeps streaming from memory.
- A card with commits from two root executions shows one icon, newest first.
- Unmerged commits from valid linked worktrees are viewable before merge; remain visible after full merge; hidden if worktree removed unmerged.
- Selecting a commit that touched the card shows a read-only body diff (first parent vs. commit) without changing dirty/autosave/history state.
- First `Escape` exits diff mode keeping popup open; second `Escape` closes popup.
- Selecting a commit that didn't touch the current card path opens other changed files without entering body diff mode.
- Other-file diff and VS Code line opening work locally and through remote control.
- Same menu/diff behavior in card popup and file mode.
- Missing bridge hides icon; malformed activity reports a visible error.
- Tests cover: stable-id storage, root/child aggregation, serialized atomic writes, single terminal conversation write, primary/worktree visibility, discarded worktree hiding, full-merge retention, missing commit, root commit, frontmatter-only diff, Escape order, both toolbar hosts, remote proxy, no live-editor persistence side effects.

## Documentation impact

Update F_050/F_012 conversation persistence wording and F_056 history ownership/storage wording. No migration or legacy schema support required.

entries.content: The failure is not a project-data error. The startup path treats an initial WebSocket connection failure as a failed project restore, while the remote-connection UI has its own retry/error flow and may immediately attempt the same connection again. I’m checking the tests and recent history to confirm whether this duplicated ownership is intentional.

Findings:

- The saved last project uses remote storage. Startup immediately attempts its stored WebSocket connection.
- If the desktop server is unavailable, the socket throws `Remote-control connection failed`.
- That expected connectivity failure bubbles into generic startup handling. `App` calls `dialogService.error`, which reports the string to Sentry. This explains the issue title and missing stack frames.
- Remote connection state and errors are already managed by `RemoteConnectionService` and the connection dialog. The global restore error is duplicate and incorrectly classified as an application failure.
- The available Sentry data cannot identify why the connection failed; likely causes include the desktop app being stopped, network interruption, or startup timing.

Proposed solution:

Treat `RemoteControlConnectionError` during last-project restoration as recoverable. Finish startup normally and let the remote connection dialog show the failure and provide retry. Do not call `dialogService.error` for this case. Add tests confirming that remote connection failures do not create a restore error or Sentry event, while genuine project restoration failures still do.

## Current state

Assigning a linked worktree to a card calls `WorktreeService.setCardWorktree`, which asks the desktop host to prepare the selected checkout. The desktop service revalidates the checkout and intentionally rejects the operation when it contains uncommitted changes. The checkout and its changes remain untouched.

`WorktreeSelector` catches the rejection and calls `dialogService.error`. That method reports every error to Sentry before showing it to the user. The expected dirty-worktree guard is therefore recorded as an application failure.

## Implementation details

Add a shared error code for the expected dirty linked-worktree condition. Set this code on the error thrown by the desktop worktree cleanliness guard. The existing bridge error envelope already preserves string error codes, so the renderer can identify the condition without matching its message.

In the worktree assignment UI, show this coded error with `dialogService.displayError`, retaining the current user-visible message without sending telemetry. Continue using `dialogService.error` for all other preparation failures.

The cleanliness guard is also used by pull, rebase, integration, conflict recovery, synchronization, and parking operations. Adding the code must preserve their current rejection behavior; this change only alters telemetry handling for the card-assignment path covered by this issue.

Add focused tests that verify the desktop rejection carries the error code, the bridge preserves it, the assignment UI displays the message without reporting telemetry, and an unexpected preparation error is still reported.

## Acceptance criteria

- Assigning a dirty linked worktree to a card is rejected before any branch switch or file change.
- The user sees that the linked worktree has uncommitted changes.
- The expected dirty-worktree rejection is not sent to Sentry from the card-assignment flow.
- Dirty-worktree checks for other worktree operations retain their existing behavior.
- Unexpected worktree preparation failures remain visible to the user and are sent to Sentry.

+## Current state
+
+When the last project uses remote storage, startup creates a `RemoteControlStorageService` and attempts to restore the WebSocket connection before opening the project. If the remote desktop is unavailable, the connection rejects with `RemoteControlConnectionError: Remote-control connection failed`.
+
+`ApplicationStartupService` treats this expected connectivity failure like any other project restoration failure. `App` then passes the composed restore message to `dialogService.error`, which reports it to Sentry. Because the reported value is a string rather than the original error, the event has no application stack frames.
+
+`RemoteConnectionService` already owns remote connection status and its user-visible error. `RemoteConnectButton` also attempts the same-origin connection when it mounts and opens its connection dialog when that attempt fails. The generic restore dialog and Sentry event therefore duplicate the remote connection flow.
+
+## Implementation details
+
+- In `ApplicationStartupService`, treat `RemoteControlConnectionError` from initial project restoration as a recoverable startup outcome. Continue startup with no restored project resolution instead of setting `bootstrap.error`.
+- Continue the remaining startup work, including the startup model-catalog refresh, after a recoverable remote connection failure.
+- Keep the error in `RemoteConnectionService`, which already publishes the disconnected state and connection message.
+- Make `RemoteConnectButton` open the remote connection dialog when it mounts with a disconnected snapshot containing an error. The existing same-origin connection attempt and manual retry behavior remain responsible for reconnecting and opening the remote project.
+- Do not suppress other project restoration errors. They must continue through the existing bootstrap error dialog and Sentry reporting path.
+- Add focused tests for recoverable remote startup failure, completion of the remaining startup work, connection-dialog presentation, retry, and continued reporting of unexpected restore failures.
+
+No desktop-host or remote-control protocol change is required.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- An unavailable remote desktop during last-project restoration does not show `Could not restore last project: Remote-control connection failed`.
+- The expected initial remote connection failure is not reported to Sentry.
+- Startup completes and the main window becomes available after the connection failure.
+- The remote connection dialog shows the connection failure and allows the user to retry.
+- A successful retry connects to the remote desktop and opens its active project through the existing flow.
+- Startup work after project restoration still runs when the remote connection is unavailable.
+- Non-connection project restoration failures retain the existing restore dialog and Sentry reporting behavior.
